_comment: EV5 — how the Meadows water LOOKS (bible §15). Geometry — the water level, the pond centre, the stream course and its carve — lives in data/config/terrain_playground.json's `water` block, because the heightfield, the terrain bake and the vegetation scatter all read it and must agree with the visual layer about where the shoreline is. Everything in THIS file is presentation and ALL of it is TUNABLE.
_comment_colours: Deep water leans on palette.json sky.day_blue's family pulled toward teal (open water reflects sky); shallow pulls toward the meadow greens so the shore shift reads as the same world, not a swimming-pool liner. fresnel_colour started as art.json's fog colour (#b9c8cf) so grazing water would meet the same sky language as the fogged hills — wrong call, own-render round 2: at any distance the viewing angle is grazing, so the WHOLE far pond takes the fresnel colour, and a near-white fresnel made distant water read as milk. It now sits between sky.day_blue and the fog colour, so far water reads as sky-blue water and only the last stretch before the horizon would fog out like everything else.
_comment_pond: The pond surface is a flat grid at the water level, trimmed to quads that touch water; the shader's per-pixel depth does the actual shoreline. `grid_step` only bounds how coarsely the trim follows the shore, not the visual waterline.
_comment_stream: The stream surface is a ribbon following the carved bed at `surface_depth` above it, clamped so it only ever descends, ending at the pond's own level. Width comes from the terrain config's stream block (the same width the carve and the scatter exclusion use).

stream._comment_alpha: Stream-only override over surface.alpha_shallow — see water.gd's build() for the measurement that split them. TUNABLE.
stream._comment_flow: EV5-remainder: the flowing-water variant. The ribbon writes its course into UV2 and the shader scrolls the wave normals downstream along it (the parameterisation IS the flow map — water.gd already computed per-sample tangents, exactly the plumbing the backlog item named). flow_speed is metres of course per second; flow_stretch < 1 elongates ripples along the flow. Both TUNABLE.
stream._comment_dressing: T1-GROUND-2. The stream had ZERO bank dressing — pond and river both get `reeds`/`bank_scrub`, the stream got neither, which is most of why a blind critic standing at its own authored bank point saw only meadow grass. `_build_plant_band` (the same function pond/river use) is gated on the member `_level`, the POND's flat surface; the stream's bed keeps falling along its own short course, so water.gd::_build_stream_reeds swaps `_level` to the LOCAL bed height at a handful of stations along the trimmed centreline instead of once for the whole body. `clumps`/`per_clump` below are deliberately small relative to river's (90/14): each station calls _build_plant_band once, the ~90m authored course trims to well under that once the head ramp and pond mouth are cut, and stations sit ~8m apart, so a river-sized clump count here would over-place badly. TUNABLE — if the bank still reads bare, raise clumps/per_clump before adding stations.

_comment_reeds: Bible §15: 'vegetation/reeds at banks'. Placed by the water composer itself — it marches the actual shoreline (the height isoline the level defines) and stands clumps in a band straddling the waterline, so the reeds always hug the real shore no matter how the level is tuned. Meshes are the SAME Quaternius wispy grass the drygrass layer uses (one nature family, D24) at taller scale and a deep marsh-green tint — a different plant read from material and context, not a new asset. NOT routed through vegetation.json because those two models already belong to the drygrass layer, and vegetation.gd groups batches by model — listing them in a second layer there silently loses one layer's tint (its own documented failure mode).

reeds._comment_gate_a_pockets: Gate A pond-side composition: concentrate the established reed clumps into four irregular bank arcs instead of distributing them around the entire large basin. The Pond Circuit arrival (-87 degrees), mill/ranger/jetty side, and departure (+35 degrees) remain inside one continuous open sector from -105 to +55 degrees; gaps between the other arcs preserve additional shoreline access. Counts make each selected arc a layered stand, not a perimeter ring. TUNABLE.
reeds._comment_stands: EV5 blind rounds 4-5 found that many small clumps spread around the whole shore read as a perimeter ring. The authored Gate A bearing arcs above now make a few real brakes with long open banks between them; the 24 clumps vary internally and only sample those pockets. Tint stays lifted from #6c8850 to #7a9460 because darker stands rendered near-black against bright water. TUNABLE.

_comment_marginals: EV5-remainder: a SECOND waterside plant silhouette beyond the wispy-grass reed — the nature pack's own broadleaf Plant_1_Big, arching over the waterline at reduced scale, in-family per D24. Same band keys as `reeds` (water.gd routes both through one builder). EV5-remainder-2: the fuller Stylized Nature MegaKit landed (d64df71) and was searched for a literal sedge/cattail model — none exists by name in any of its 270 files. Grass_Wheat is the closest available read: a tall, narrow, dense blade-cluster mesh with a distinct seed-head silhouette (1.11x1.78x1.01m raw bbox, 1530 verts) genuinely distinct from Plant_1_Big's broad arching leaf (2.89x3.76x3.13m, 360 verts) — reuses the already-staged Grass.png texture, a plain vertical gradient strip fully controlled by this band's own tint. ALL TUNABLE, including whether Grass_Wheat should get its own tint/scale split from Plant_1_Big's if a verify pass flags a proportion mismatch.

marginals._comment_gate_a_pockets: Broadleaf and wheat silhouettes sit inside the larger reed arcs so the banks layer from low water grass to taller marginal plants instead of repeating one silhouette everywhere. Narrower ranges leave visible reed-only edges around each pocket. TUNABLE.

_comment_bank_flowers: Gate A: ankle-height warm flower groups on the dry lip of selected reed pockets. This reuses the existing Meadows flower family at its established 0.07-0.26 scale, and uses the shore's actual height isoline rather than hand-placing blooms at coordinates that would drift when the basin is tuned.
_comment_dressing: EV5-remainder: the aquatic dressing eight blind rounds converged asking for — all from packs already staged and ledgered (searched before treating anything as blocked): Rock_Medium boulders half-submerged, Pebble_Round scaled up into smooth shore stones, the Kenney logs (ledger: 'retained for the log shapes') beached as driftwood, Plant_7's flat rosette floating as lily pads. Counts, depth bands, scales, sinks ALL TUNABLE. Boulders collide (vegetation.gd's hologram/camera lesson); stones are shin-height and do not.

boulders._comment_tint: Own-render pass: untinted, the pack's bluish rock texture rendered as pale baby-blue crowns against the water — a warm grey multiply lands them in the same family as the hillside scatter's retinted rocks. TUNABLE.

driftwood._comment_tint: Own-render pass: the Kenney log's cream vertex colours multiply through the batch tint, so it is authored darker than the target weathered grey-brown. TUNABLE.

lilypads._comment_tint: Own-render pass: at #4f7d44 the pad clusters read as near-black clumps on the bright water; lifted a step. TUNABLE.

_comment_jetty: EV5-remainder, the key art's jetty: a short working deck where the pond path meets the water (bearing_deg is the bearing OUT of the pond centre toward the path's arrival side; water.gd finds the actual shoreline crossing itself, so retuning the water level moves the jetty with the shore). Village-kit modules only (D24): Floor_WoodDark deck, WoodenFence railing, Kenney-log pilings, EV7's crate and bucket at the end. deck_above_water and land_overlap in metres. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_round1: EV5 authoring round 1 (own read of the first render, before any blind round): the pond rendered as pale milk with a solid white shoreline ring. Foam rebalanced in the shader (noise now required, contact alone cannot clear the threshold) and the height texture went R8 -> RF (see water.gd's _bake_height_texture for the staircase this removed). Here: deep colour darker and reached sooner (depth_falloff 1.6->1.2), alpha_deep 0.88->0.93 so the bright sandy bed stops lifting the deep water, fresnel wash cut (0.65->0.4, power 4->5), wave normals calmed (0.35->0.22), roughness up a step so the sun sheen stops frosting the whole surface. ALL still TUNABLE.
_comment_round2: EV5 blind round 1 (first genuinely blind critique, fresh headless session, no context): verbatim defects and the levers moved — 'swimming-pool cyan against olive land' -> deep/shallow/fresnel all pulled toward the keyart's warm teal-green family; 'shallow-to-deep gradient is a constant-width ring, not depth' -> depth_falloff 1.2->2.2 so the ramp spreads wide on shallow banks and stays narrow on steep ones; 'no sun glint... unfinished' -> roughness back to 0.10, shader SPECULAR restored to 0.5, wave normals up 0.22->0.4 and finer (uv_scale 0.09->0.12); 'foam is a bead chain' -> foam_scale down plus a second decorrelating noise scale in the shader; 'one reed asset, one scale... on the sand, not in the water' -> band reaches 0.55m BELOW the waterline, scale span widened, per-instance lean/tone jitter in water.gd. Reflections are the one named defect deliberately NOT chased: bible sec15 forbids the expensive tier, gl_compatibility has no SSR, and a planar reflection probe is exactly the simulation the spec rules out — fresnel-toward-sky is this tier's honest ceiling, recorded in DONE.md rather than faked. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_round3: EV5 blind round 2: the two water-scope defects still actionable at this tier were the depth ramp's mach banding (dithered in the shader now) and the stream reading as a different, darker water than the pond -- the stream's read is its dark pebble bed showing through shallow water at grazing angle, so alpha_shallow comes up 0.42->0.52 (the surface's own colour carries more of both waters) and the stream rides 0.35 above its bed instead of 0.45, which shifts its depth colour toward the pond's shallow family. Round 2 also asked for CONTINUOUS rim foam -- the exact 'drawn ring' round 1 condemned; the two critics disagree and the broken-lap read stays, recorded here so a future pass doesn't ping-pong. 'No reflections' repeats from round 1 and stays the recorded ceiling of this tier: bible sec15 rules out the expensive route and gl_compatibility has no SSR; fresnel-toward-sky is the honest substitute. A pond OUTLET (round 2, real hydrology note) is Band 3's river's natural starting point -- see DONE.md's EV5 entry. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_round4: EV5 blind round 3: two NEW water-scope defects and one root cause found by CPU-replicating the shader. The 'stream is a different water' complaint from rounds 1-3 was never colour tuning -- the depth texture's fixed level±8m window clamped every texel more than 8m above the pond, so the upper stream computed ~5m of phantom depth and rendered the deep colour (see water.gd's height_min/max scan comment). With that fixed, round-3 asks land as: ripple normals now attenuate with camera distance in the shader (far sheen scattered into a 'flat cyan fill' read), shallow colour pulled a step deeper/greener toward the board and its alpha trimmed so the sunlit sand bed stops lifting the whole pond toward tropical cyan, and the reed band above the waterline tightened 0.45->0.28m so stands stop straying onto dry lawn. Round 3 also asked for foam 'continuous or removed' -- the third different foam verdict in three rounds; the broken-lap middle stays. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_rounds5_8: EV5 blind rounds 5-8 (each a fresh, context-free session). Round 5: no new in-scope defect. Round 6: 'glass cards' = submerged grass tufts read as artifacts -> grass min_height pulled to ankle depth (vegetation.json); reed perimeter-ring note acted on (see _comment_stands). Round 7: repeats and two verified misreads ('water plane escaping the bank' is the pond's own west arm behind a low sand spit, checked by crop; 'butt-joint' is the drone angle). Round 8: judged identical frames, no new in-scope defect -> two consecutive flat rounds, CONVERGED per ralph/conventions.md's stopping rule. Bar question B (same kind of game as the references) flipped to a qualified YES in rounds 7 and 8, carried by the water frames. What the critics still name, recorded as the wall rather than chased: real reflections/refraction/caustics (bible sec15's own 'no physically expensive simulation' line, and gl_compatibility has no SSR -- fresnel-toward-sky is this tier's ceiling); aquatic dressing that needs assets not in the build (lily pads, driftwood, jetty, submerged-rock meshes); and world-level gaps outside EV5 entirely (sky/clouds/haze, near-field ground-cover density, canopy-scale trees, creature/trainer art, the perimeter's placeholder slabs). Foam received five contradictory verdicts across eight rounds (broken/continuous/remove/depth-driven[it is]/fixed-offset[it isn't]); the broken-lap treatment stands.
_comment_river: SE21 -- how the RIVER looks. Its geometry (course, per-point depth and width, water level) is in terrain_playground.json's `river` block for the same reason the pond's is: the heightfield cuts the channel from it and this file only says what the water on top looks like. The surface reuses the same shader and the same material builder as the pond, over its OWN region rect. ALL TUNABLE.

river._comment_sample_step: Metres between ribbon stations along the 340m course. Each station measures its own waterline outward from the centreline, so this also sets how closely the water's edge follows a meander.
river._comment_alpha: Between the pond's 0.48 and the stream's 0.78. The channel is raw cut earth 6-9m under the surface through the middle reaches; at the pond's alpha the whole river read as its own dark bed seen through glass, which is the measurement EV5 already made once when it split the stream's alpha off.
river._comment_flow: A big river runs slower than the brook (1.1) and its ripples are longer. Direction is the course's own authored order -- north, off the rise's flank, to the southern ring.

reeds._comment: Anchors come from the river's own measured waterline (both banks, every station), so `clumps` is spread over ~680m of bank rather than the pond's ~300m -- hence the count. max_bank_slope_deg is high because a river bank IS steep here (70-80 degrees, measured): the pond's 33 would reject every anchor and place nothing at all.

bank_scrub._comment: The band that makes the river read from 150m out. `band_below` is NEGATIVE on purpose -- the arithmetic in _build_plant_band is `skip if ground < level - band_below`, so -0.6 means 'start 0.6m ABOVE the water' and nothing is placed in the river itself. Scrub rather than trees: this band has no collision (it is the pond's reed mechanism), and a tree standing on the walkable rim that a player can walk through is exactly OF14's defect. The tree line either side of the channel comes for free instead -- vegetation.gd's own slope rule keeps trees off the 70-degree walls and lands them on the rims.
